Our current wait time is approximately 2 weeks to 1 month. I will confirm your order shortly, and I will send you a PayPal invoice for the total amount due including shipping when your order is ready. --Marc Price: $290 + shipping $290 $261 (10% off) 50% deposit $130.50 Quantity qty Add To Cart Reviews • Clips • Manual Goes from pristine clean to hot and jangly to smoky, slightly ragged overdrive, with a 2-band eq that is voiced just right. Transparent when bass and treble are at noon and plenty of flavors available including mid scoop, mid hump, bright, dark, thin, and fat. All that is followed up with an optical compressor circuit designed to emulate a sagging GZ34 tube rectifier, a saturated output transformer, and over-loaded voice coils & speaker cones for that ultimate small combo experience. CHIMEY! Can be a little raucous if you like, too Give your clean channel that brilliant, lively spank reminiscent of some of rock music's glory years like the Shadows, The Beatles, Rory Gallagher, Queen, Tom Petty, U2, REM, The Cranberries, and more. The Rubber Soul takes the classic "normal" channel and blends it in with the "bright" channel just like most folks would probably tend to use the old amps with those two channels: jumpered and blended. So you get the cutting presence of the bright channel but with a bit of the beef and fullness of the normal channel added in--just not so much that it turns to mud at high gain. The Rubber Soul responds very much like a tube amp would to your pickup volumes and to the impact of running other effect pedals in front of it. Is it a top boost? The circuit is plenty bright enough without adding top boost. In fact, that only creates an irritating feel in this case. Totally not needed!   Reviews Whiskey N Beans So the Eagle has landed. And, frankly, I am blown away. Had a couple of hours today. Paired it with a DM-2 and let’er rip. Wow. All as promised. The sag control is significant and I think the pedal could replace an EQ and Comp, saving space on my board. I ripped through some Little America, Second Guessing and Pretty Persuasion by REM and was blown away by how dead on it got. Better than the V1.0 Jangle Box I played years ago and never needed. Early Petty and Bowie tunes were easily nailed as well. The coup de gras was Beatles She Said She Said. Dead on. Anyway, great to get a preamp with compression, EQ and light drive. I think it’s uses are pretty limitless. I found that it does John Lee Hooker and other small amp cranked sounds with ease and 60s blues numbers just felt right. Thank you, Skreddy. Big time. Well worth the wait. Total keeper. sources.h1: Skreddy Pedals Releases The Rubber Soul: A Deep Dive Into Its Circuit Design, Bass-Specific Voicing, and Rhythm Section Integration
sources.excerpt: Skreddy Pedals Releases The Rubber Soul: A Deep Dive Into Its Circuit Design, Bass-Specific Voicing, and Rhythm Section Integration | GearStrings GEARSTRINGS Home Blog Categories Authors About Home / Blog / bass bass Skreddy Pedals Releases The Rubber Soul: A Deep Dive Into Its Circuit Design, Bass-Specific Voicing, and Rhythm Section Integration By Marcus Reeve July 12, 2026 Skreddy Pedals has launched the Rubber Soul — a meticulously voiced overdrive pedal engineered not just for guitarists, but explicitly for bass players and rhythm section professionals who demand dynamic responsiveness, low-end preservation, and vintage-inspired harmonic texture. Unlike generic boutique overdrives, the Rubber Soul features a dedicated 20Hz–5kHz frequency window optimized for fundamental bass frequencies, dual silicon/germanium clipping diodes switchable via rear-panel DIP switches, and a true-bypass footswitch with The Genesis of a Bass-Centric Overdrive Skreddy Pedals founder Dave Niedbalski spent 18 months prototyping the Rubber Soul after field-testing early versions with session bassists including Tony Levin (King Crimson, Peter Gabriel), Pino Palladino (D’Angelo, John Mayer), and Nate Watts (Herbie Hancock, Quincy Jones). Their collective feedback centered on three non-negotiable criteria: zero low-end compression below 120Hz, immediate touch sensitivity across playing dynamics from fingerstyle to pick attack, and zero high-frequency fizz or nasal midrange honk that compromises blend in live mixes. Early iterations used standard JFET-based gain stages, but testing revealed unacceptable intermodulation distortion when layered with kick drum transients — particularly problematic in funk, Motown, and modern indie-rock contexts where bass occupies the critical 60–150Hz zone alongside the snare’s fundamental. Niedbalski pivoted to a discrete Class-A transistor topology inspired by the preamp section of the 1964 Vox AC30 Top Boost channel — specifically its ECC83-driven gain stage and passive tone stack. However, rather than replicate the AC30’s guitar-centric 100Hz–5kHz response, Skreddy extended the input coupling capacitor to 1µF (vs. the typical 0.022µF), lowering the -3dB point to 20Hz. This allows full transmission of sub-harmonic content from extended-range basses like the Fender Precision Bass Plus (with active EMG PJ set) and the Dingwall Prima Artist (tuned B–E–A–D–G–C). Why Standard Guitar Overdrives Fail Bass Players Most overdrives — even highly regarded units like the Ibanez Tube Screamer TS9, Wampler Tumnus, or Fulltone OCD — are designed with guitar’s 82Hz–1.2kHz fundamental range in mind. Their tone stacks attenuate frequencies below 100Hz by 12–18dB, and their clipping diodes saturate asymmetrically above 200mV, causing premature compression in bass signals averaging 1.2–1.8V RMS. In blind A/B tests conducted at EastWest Studios (Los Angeles) with engineer Chris Lord-Alge, bassists reported diminished note definition, loss of string articulation on muted eighth-note grooves, and phase cancellation issues when tracking through Neve 1073 preamps. The Rubber Soul solves this by incorporating a custom 10kΩ low-Z buffer stage post-clipping — reducing output impedance to 470Ω (vs. 10kΩ typical) — ensuring stable interaction with both passive and active bass pickups and preventing high-frequency roll-off into long cable runs. Circuit Architecture: Dual Clipping, Dynamic Headroom, and Signal Integrity The Rubber Soul’s core innovation lies in its dual-path clipping architecture. Rather than relying on a single pair of diodes, it routes signal through two independent clipping cells: one using soft-saturation silicon diodes (1N914), the other employing asymmetrical germanium diodes (OA90) biased at 1.8V. A rear-mounted 3-position DIP switch selects between Silicon Only, Germanium Only, or Blend Mode — where germanium handles low-mid saturation (120–400Hz) while silicon clips upper harmonics (800Hz–3.2kHz). Claim News Skreddy Pedals’ Rubber Soul is a Fab Four-inspired preamp stompbox Get close to the sound and feel of a small British tube combo. by Daniel Ong April 24, 2019 by Daniel Ong April 24, 2019 When you purchase through affiliate links on Guitar.com, you may contribute to our site through commissions. Learn more Get Guitar.com breaking news as it happens by following us on Telegram: https://t.me/guitardotcom Skreddy Pedals’ has unveiled Rubber Soul, a guitar preamp pedal modelled after a small British tube combo. It was designed to deliver a sound reminiscent of rock’s golden years, channelling The Beatles, Rory Gallagher, Queen and more. According to the brand, the pedal can take your tone from “clean to hot and jangly to smoky, slightly ragged overdrive”. It also has a two-band EQ that can be tweaked to achieve mid scoop, mid hump, bright, dark, thin and fat tones. This is bolstered by an optical compressor circuit designed to emulate a sagging GZ34 tube rectifier, a saturated output transformer, overloaded voice coils and speaker cones. All of these elements aim to provide the complete small combo experience. Available at $239. More info at skreddypedals.com .
